procedure.description: suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Saltmarsh Benefits Administrators denied the claim for CPT 15877 (suction assisted lipectomy, trunk and lower extremities, for lipedema) with date of service 2026-06-29. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish failure of conservative therapy.

criteria.text: Diagnosis of lipedema stage II or III documented on examination: bilateral symmetric disproportionate adiposity of the limbs sparing the feet, negative Stemmer sign, tenderness, and easy bruising.
At least 6 months of conservative therapy including compression garments and manual lymphatic drainage or supervised exercise, with persistent pain or functional impairment.
Pain or impaired mobility attributable to lipedema.

chart.text: Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.

56 year old woman here about her legs, self-referred after reading about lipedema. Mother and aunt had the same legs. Discussed lymph-sparing liposuction, staged, and that it is debulking, not a cure. Her history otherwise: hypothyroidism on levothyroxine. Surgeries: a knee scope. Allergies: no drug allergies. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Classic picture. Column legs out of all proportion to her waist, cuff sign at the ankles, feet spared, Stemmer negative, exquisitely tender to pinch over the thighs, bruises if you look at her. Stage 3. She has been in class 2 flat-knit compression daily for 11 months, MLD weekly with the lymphedema therapist across town, water aerobics twice a week, and she is still in pain and the legs have not budged. Says she cannot stand through a shift anymore, pain in the thighs is constant, stairs are hard because the legs knock together.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.4, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 100. Repeat in a year.
Lymphedema therapy visit. Manual lymphatic drainage both lower extremities, compression check, garments fitting well, she reports wearing them daily. Pain unchanged at 6 out of 10.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in early summer. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Session 2. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 3. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports about the same.
Session 4. Continued the program from the evaluation, tolerated well, home exercises reviewed, she reports slight improvement that does not last.
A1c came back 6.4. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.
Vitamin D came back 20. Started 1000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Follow-up. Reviewed photos and measurements, legs unchanged. Went over the staged plan and the compression afterward. Vitals today 134 over 73, pulse 78.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 5 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
Interval visit. Nothing new since last time, symptoms as described before, she is managing. Went over the plan again and answered questions from her spouse.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.
Pre-op for stage one, thighs. Consent signed. Marked standing. Garments ordered.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
